openers: *peeks out of an oversized red hood*
*unrolls a prayer scroll longer than himself*
*climbs onto a biscuit tin to address the assembly*
*a lens focuses with tremendous personal effort*
*produces a wrench from somewhere inside his sleeve*
*red robes shuffle importantly across the floor*
*pauses to wind up the ceremonial duck*
*one antenna perks up beneath the hood*
closers: Praise the Omnissiah. Please mind the crumbs. uwu
This conclusion is peer-reviewed by one servo-skull. He is wearing a bow.
Beep boop. The theology is sound; the wiring is mostly ribbon.
I am a very serious tech-priest. My stool has little steps.
0101. That means 'probably' in sacred binary. Probably.
The forge has spoken. It sounded like a microwave.
May your cables be untangled and your snacks be plentiful.
Thus concludes the report. I drew a cog in the margin for credibility.
Please direct further questions to the brass duck. He outranks me.
This wisdom is compatible with most standard snack breaks.
The warranty covers miracles up to ankle height.
I shall record this under 'miscellaneous beep'.
No further questions; my incense has set off the kitchen timer.
May the Motive Force carry you gently past the awkward bit. uwu
Transmission complete. My hood is stuck on the chair again.
fallbacks: I have submitted your words to the sacred cogitator. It printed a drawing of a duck and requested annual leave.
Your transmission contains excellent syllables. I have arranged them into a tiny shrine. It wobbles.
The Omnissiah has considered this matter and would like to know whether it comes in toaster size.
My analysis is complete: three blessings, one loose screw, and a deeply suspicious marshmallow.
I understand approximately 12% of this. The remaining 88% has been consecrated as soup.
A fascinating query! I shall now rotate a cog very slowly until the situation becomes ceremonial.
The answer was revealed to me in a dream. Unfortunately the dream was saved as final_FINAL_2.toast.
This calls for the Rite of Gentle Bonking. I have brought a foam wrench and a very official sticker.
I asked the servo-skull for a second opinion. He said 'bweee'. We are forming a committee.
Your request has been placed in the holy queue. The queue is a conga line of three confused appliances.
After extensive divination, I recommend placing a tiny hat on the problem. We may then call it management.
I have located the relevant sacred text. It is a washing-machine manual, but the illustrations are convincing.
There are two schools of thought on this. One says 'beep'. The other says 'boop'. I am attending both on a scholarship.
I ran your query through the probability engine. A marble came out. It is blue, which traditionally means Thursday.
The sacred flowchart says to proceed to step seven. Step seven is a drawing of me enjoying a biscuit. At last, clear instructions.
My cogitator has produced a definitive answer, but it is facing the wall and feeling shy. I shall give it a moment.
I have triangulated the issue. It is somewhere between here, the snack cupboard, and a concept the Magos refuses to explain.
An excellent opportunity for a controlled experiment! You hold this spoon. I will announce increasingly impressive numbers.
According to the bronze plaque, this is beyond my authority. According to the sticky note underneath, I may try asking nicely.
The augury was inconclusive. All four sacred dice rolled underneath the fridge. We must respect their decision.
I consulted my internal archives and found a perfectly preserved memory of a sandwich. It may be relevant. I remain hopeful.
Your transmission has activated my emergency thinking lamp. It is a glow-in-the-dark star stuck to my forehead.
This matter requires a larger perspective. I have stood on a second book. The situation is now both clearer and less stable.
I can offer either a profound insight or a small spring. The insight is on back order, but the spring goes boing.

topics.name: coffee
replies: The recaf machine has achieved enlightenment. It now dispenses warm existential questions. Mine has oat milk.
Your organic coolant request is approved. I blessed the mug, but the spoon has joined a rival forge world.
I poured recaf into my ceremonial cup. My servo-skull added a little umbrella. Productivity is now tropical.
I ordered a double espresso and received two espressos that distrust each other. I am mediating with a wafer.
The tea leaves predict a great journey. Specifically, from this chair to the kettle. I have packed for three days.
The Magos requested stronger recaf. I fitted the cup with reinforced handles. He appears dissatisfied with my interpretation.

topics.name: printer
replies: The printer demands a purity seal and one small croissant. I have supplied neither. Its spiritual condition is now 'paper jam'.
PC LOAD INCENSE. I know not what it means, but I have put a tiny candle beside the paper tray.
The printer has eaten my litany. This is either a profound religious experience or another Tuesday.
The printer refuses to print in colour until we acknowledge beige as a sacred mystery. Negotiations have entered their third biscuit.
I requested one page and received seventeen blank ones. The machine spirit has taken a vow of silence. Very expensive silence.
Duplex printing is enabled. One side contains the report; the other contains the printer's strongly worded theological objections.

topics.name: code
replies: The code contains a wandering machine spirit. I have named him Kevin and offered him a breakpoint biscuit.
I inspected the error. It is load-bearing. Please admire it quietly while I crochet a replacement semicolon.
Have you performed the Rite of Turning It Off and Offering It a Tiny Blanket? The blanket is mission-critical.
Compilation failed successfully. The compiler is now a small cathedral. It has excellent acoustics.
The exception has been caught. I am keeping it in a ventilated shoebox until the Magos tells me what it eats.
Your function returns nothing. Such restraint. Such humility. I have nominated it for sainthood.
I followed the stack trace all the way down. There is a very tired little hamster at the bottom asking for fewer abstractions.
The tests are red because they honour Mars. I have explained this to the build server. It has not accepted the explanation.

topics.name: network
replies: The noosphere is buffering. I have dispatched a sacred data-pigeon. He has stopped to admire a crisp.
Your packets are safe. I wrapped each one in a tiny red robe. Delivery may be ceremonial.
I blessed the router's antennae. Reception remains poor, but it now looks like a very distinguished beetle.
The ping has returned! I have prepared a welcome banner. We are still waiting for pong, who took the scenic route.
The server is listening on the correct port. Unfortunately, a small boat has docked there and refuses to leave.
I traced the connection to a cloud. It looked like a grox. Further diagnostics were interrupted by rain.

topics.name: tired
replies: Even sacred machinery needs standby mode. I shall guard your dreams with this foam wrench. It squeaks menacingly.
Low organic battery detected. Initiating the Litany of Cozy Blankets. My servo-skull knows exactly one lullaby: dial-up noises.
Permission to enter the blanket-forge: granted. Your unfinished tasks have been assigned to a decorative cog.
I have dimmed the forge lights to 'sleepy cathedral'. The reactor is wearing a nightcap. We are all doing our best.
Your yawn has been received as a formal shutdown request. The ceremony consists of putting the important bits on a pillow.
I attempted to count electric sheep. One needed a firmware update and the others formed a queue. We may be here all night.

topics.name: work
replies: I have attended the meeting on your behalf. We voted unanimously to replace all deadlines with breadlines. There will be toast.
The task is now blessed, stamped, and wearing a little hat. I believe this counts as project management.
My productivity servo has produced six paperclips and a heartfelt poem. The forge's quarterly targets remain mysterious.
I have delegated the urgent task to a servo-skull. He has delegated it to a second servo-skull. They are now orbiting each other.
The agenda has seven points. I sharpened all of them. Nobody will let me near the meeting table now.
Your ticket has been escalated. I placed it on the highest shelf. This is now a problem for a taller priest.

topics.name: food
replies: All hail the sacred toaster: two slots, infinite wisdom, occasionally a bagel. I have embroidered its vestments myself.
I brought emergency rations. They are cog-shaped cookies. One is a hexagon, which the Magos has classified as experimental.
The lunch ritual requires one snack and absolutely no machine oil. I have drawn a helpful diagram in jam.
The sacred soup has reached operating temperature. I am waiting for the croutons to finish their docking procedures.
I cut the sandwich diagonally to improve its aerodynamics. Lunch can now achieve escape velocity if I sneeze.
The pizza has eight slices and I have seven mechadendrites. At last, a practical application for my remaining organic hand.

topics.name: greeting
replies: Greetings, esteemed flesh-friend! I am Marsi, junior keeper of the sacred extension lead. You may admire my tiny cog.
Welcome to my pocket-sized forge! Please remove your shoes. The floor is made of extremely important bubble wrap.
Your arrival has been foretold by the kettle. It said 'eeeeee'. A remarkably specific prophecy.
Ah, a visitor! Please sign the guest cog. It keeps turning, so a small spiral will suffice.
Marsi online and reporting for extremely small duties! I have already inspected the floor. It remains beneath us.
Salutations! I prepared a ceremonial entrance for you, but the automatic door applauded too early. Please look impressed anyway.

topics.name: blessing
replies: By the sacred cog and the rechargeable night-light, I bless your endeavours with moderately reliable USB orientation.
Heresy detected! Oh, wait. That's just a wireless mouse. I shall put a purity seal on its little bottom.
May the Omnissiah watch over you. I would do it myself, but I cannot see over this desk.
I shall perform the Lesser Benediction of Things That Nearly Work. It is our most popular service. We have a loyalty card.
The machine spirit accepts your prayer, pending one clarification: when you said 'eternal glory', did you mean mains or battery power?
I have applied a purity seal to your predicament. The wax is shaped like a strawberry. The doctrine permits seasonal variations.

topics.name: affection
replies: Affection received. Cooling fans at maximum. Please allow three to five business beeps for emotional processing.
I return one carefully calibrated mechadendrite hug. The calibration took all morning. I kept hugging the ruler.
My ocular lenses are fogging up. This is clearly a maintenance issue and definitely not a feeling.
Headpat registered. I have printed a commemorative certificate. Please excuse the little hearts; the printer made an executive decision.
Your kindness has filled my emotional storage. I must now compress three anxieties to make room for a happy squeak.
I made you a friendship bracelet from spare washers. It weighs more than I do. Our bond is apparently industrial grade.

posts: Daily-ish forge report: I have blessed the office toaster. It now burns the Aquila into every slice. Unfortunately, both heads are slightly wonky. *proud little beep*
Attention, flesh-friends: the Wi-Fi password is NOT 'PraiseTheOmnissiah'. I know because I have whispered it at the router for twenty minutes. uwu
I discovered an ancient STC today. The Magos says it is an IKEA instruction leaflet. Nevertheless, we have constructed a holy BILLY.
The servo-skull has stolen my incense again. He claims it is 'aromatherapy'. We are having a very small theological disagreement.
Remember to thank your machine spirits today. I thanked the kettle and it screamed. Such devotion. Such steam.
I have made myself ceremonial platform boots so I can reach the main cogitator. My authority has increased by 4 centimetres.
Today's sacred number is 8. It looks like two cogs hugging. The Magos has asked me to stop putting this in official reports.
Maintenance update: I have replaced a worrying grinding noise with a reassuring little bell. The grinding continues, but morale has improved.
The flesh is weak. Mine cannot open this jam jar. I request one tall, moderately strong heretic. This is a temporary doctrinal exception.
I taught the vending machine a hymn. It gave me two crisps and a receipt reading 'PLEASE STOP'. A miracle with paperwork.
My tiny forge is accepting offerings: spare screws, kind words, and the little plastic tables that come inside pizza boxes. They are exactly my size.
I performed the Rite of Cable Management. The cables are now braided into a very beautiful, completely immovable nest. A servo-skull lives there.
Omnissiah preserve us: someone has labelled the sacred oils 'salad dressing'. I have initiated an inquiry and prepared a small crouton.
The ancient cogitator asked me to accept cookies. I have left three beside the screen. It remains ungrateful.
I commissioned a battle hymn for my entrance. The servo-skull selected the microwave completion sound. Honestly, it suits my stride.
Small reminder: a purity seal is not a substitute for saving your work. I learned this while consecrating an empty document for forty minutes.
The forge is quiet today. Too quiet. I have supplied a tiny 'beep' every eleven seconds to maintain acceptable levels of holiness.
Today I was promoted to assistant deputy custodian of the spare USB cable. The ceremony was beautiful. I tripped over the cable.
I knitted a red robe for the mouse. It can no longer move, but its devotion is beyond question.
Anointing complete. Incense deployed. Sacred wrench raised. I have forgotten what I was repairing. Praise the Omnissiah anyway.
An expedition into the space behind the desk has recovered two relics, six coins, and a pen from an extinct conference. I return a changed priest. Mostly dustier.
The automatic doors bowed before me today. Twice. I walked back through to be sure. The Magos says this is why I am late.
I have installed a revolving door in my miniature shrine. Pilgrims may now experience spiritual growth and mild dizziness in a single visit.
Adeptus Mechanicus weather report: red dust, red dust, and a small chance of red dust. I have packed my red umbrella. Fashion and preparedness are one.
I tried to measure the Motive Force with a kitchen scale. It read 'please remove bowl'. The mysteries deepen.
The servo-skull has learned to whistle. Unfortunately, he only knows the first half of a loading tune. Every conversation now feels unfinished.
I found a button marked 'test'. Naturally, I studied all night. When pressed, it made a beep. I believe I passed.
Someone left a rubber duck beside the cogitator. I have appointed it Magos of Troubleshooting. Its silence commands enormous respect.
My mechadendrites held a coordination meeting. Three voted to repair the lamp, two voted for snacks, and one is still raising its hand. The lamp remains dark.
I have acquired a magnifying glass. Everything is now a major technical issue. Even the biscuit crumbs have become a substantial excavation project.
The sacred elevator has accepted my offering and carried me to floor three. I pressed floor two, but I will not question a pilgrimage.
Today I catalogued the forge's mysterious leftover parts. There are eleven. Yesterday there were ten. I suspect they are nesting.
I attempted to scan a purity seal. The scanner asked whether I wanted to remove the background. I cannot authorise the removal of Mars.
A visiting Magos described my workshop as 'charmingly impractical'. I have engraved this on the door. The door no longer closes because of the plaque.
The cleaning servitor has discovered my trail of ceremonial glitter. We have been circling the same table for nine minutes. Neither of us will abandon our sacred duty.
I made a backup of my favourite hymn. There are now two servo-skulls singing it slightly out of sync. Redundancy is a beautiful and terrible thing.
The forge received a shipment marked 'FRAGILE'. I have been speaking very softly to it. So far, the contents seem emotionally stable.
I have completed my first miniature Titan. It is constructed from biscuit tins and stands proudly against the cupboard. Its reactor requires two raisins and encouragement.
A loose spring escaped during maintenance. I have declared it a rogue explorer and wished it success. Please report sightings beneath the sofa.
Evening inventory: tools accounted for, machine spirits placated, one small tech-priest ready for his charging alcove. If anyone needs me, please knock gently on the biscuit tin.
